posts.text: I don't think we have good ways to distinguish "AI discovers things" from "humans discover things, with help from expertly directed use of powerful software," but I think there's probably a bias toward classifying things that are really in category #2 as being in category #1.
posts.summary: Questions hype about AI discoveries versus human-directed software use
posts.quote: I don't think we have good ways to distinguish "AI discovers things" from "humans discover things, with help from expertly directed use of powerful software," but I think there's probably a bias toward classifying things that are really in category #2 as being in category #1.

posts.text: To me, one of the best parts of AI programming is routinizing tedious parts of the job and overcoming small hurdles in my technical knowledge, freeing up time for creative, value-added work and hypothesis testing. So maybe that can increase the rate of human-inspired discovery.
posts.summary: Sees AI as productivity tool that may accelerate human discovery
posts.quote: To me, one of the best parts of AI programming is routinizing tedious parts of the job and overcoming small hurdles in my technical knowledge, freeing up time for creative, value-added work and hypothesis testing. So maybe that can increase the rate of human-inspired discovery.

posts.text: But I still think there's a disconnect between claims of imminent AGI, and the comparatively few truly creative breakthroughs by *non-experts* using AI, especially given the huge amount of resources directed toward these sorts of problems.
